rule: a receiver whose type is given by a declaration — local, parameter, field/property (including `$var->prop` / `obj.field` chains whose property has a declared type), catch parameter, for-loop variable, pattern binding — or by `= new T(...)` gives `T#m` (high if defined in the scan, else medium). | **Rust constructors type their binding**: `let x = T { .. }` and `let x = T::new(..)` / `T::default()` / `T::with_capacity(..)` give `x` type T
spec_gap: Does a Zig local without a type annotation get its type from its initializer — `const a = Point.init(1)` (an in-scan fn whose declared return type is Point) or `const b = Point{ .x = 2 }` (a struct literal)? Decision A lists receivers typed 'by a declaration … or by `= new T(...)`', and only Rust has a ruling that constructors type their binding. If yes, `a.len()`/`b.len()` are `app.Point#len` high; if no, they are `a.len`/`b.len` low. This is the dominant Zig idiom (`var list = std.ArrayList(u8).init(a)`).
notes: The edges app.run → app.Point#init (method, high, line 14) are certain under either reading.
